pr_body:
The response of the health API grows when the diagnosis is performed due to the diagnosis currently reporting all affected resources. In particular, the payload can grow by a few MB/ returned diagnosis when 50k indices are affected.

Tested this with `61_000` unassigned primary shards and `100_000` unassigned replica shards. The response size was `10MB`. The chunked response came back in about 7 seconds, degrading to about 20 seconds over 100 consecutive requests as the GC pressure increased, whilst the full response (non-chunked) came back in 25 seconds degrading to 45-50 seconds.

Fixes #90223

issue_context.title: Health API chunked response
issue_context.body:
### Description

The health API response can become a few MBs (2-3MB if 50K indices are affected).

In less extreme situations the response can be in the 10s/100s of KB. 

It might be worthwhile looking into chunking its response (this might provide clients with a better experience too)

review_comments:
Would it be possible to use the 
```java
Iterators.concat(
  diagnosisList.stream().map(ChunkedToXContent::toXContentChunked).toArray(Iterator[]::new)
);
```
pattern here instead of using Spliterators? I wonder if this concat method would be more readable than the spliterator route? I assume there's no performance concern since the same pattern was used in another chunked object already.

> I assume there's no performance concern

I think there would be. Spliterators splits the underlying (flatted) iterator into batches (see `trySplit`), whilst `Iterators.concat` doesn't. 

I'd rather we keep it like this as the affected resources in particular would benefit from batching
I think the previously asked `Iterators.concat` pattern question applies here as well?
